desc: Implement perimeter mapping: bottom edge (y=0): p=x; right edge (x=side): p=side+y; top edge (y=side): p=2*side+(side-x); left edge (x=0): p=3*side+(side-y). Sort positions.

Implement feasibility check can(D): for each start index i, greedily select next point with arc distance ≥ D using bisect on doubled array (pos + [p+P]), stop when k selected or window exceeded; require last_selected - first ≤ P - D so wrap-around gap ≥ D. Return True if any start yields k points.
Implement binary search over D in [1, 4*side // k] returning max feasible D.

Validate: run the three provided examples (expect 2, 1, 1) and a brute-force verifier on small random inputs (exhaustive subset check vs. binary-search answer) to confirm the arc-gap ⟺ Manhattan lemma for D ≤ side.

Finalize code in starter format with `from typing import List`, tight inner loops (early exit once k reached), and comment explaining the key lemma (k ≥ 4 ⟹ D ≤ side; same/adjacent edges: Manhattan = arc; opposite edges: Manhattan ≥ side ≥ D).
